deep.reconstruction:
Context (from p.224, Problem 60): find two rational right triangles, generated by (p,q) and (r,s), whose areas A = pq(p^2-q^2) and B = rs(r^2-s^2) are in a given ratio a:b. Euler says no direct method works. He therefore makes linear substitutions r = alpha*p + beta*q, s = gamma*p + delta*q. These make B share three of the four linear factors p, q, p-q, p+q with A. The equation A/B = a/b then becomes linear in p:q. Cases I-VII are on p.224; this page finishes cases VIII-X, tabulates all ten, and works examples.

Case VIII: r = p-q, s = 2q.
- Then r+s = p+q and r-s = p-3q, so B = 2q(p-q)(p+q)(p-3q).
- A/B = p/(2p-6q) = a/b, so bp = 2ap - 6aq and p/q = 6a/(2a-b).
- Take p = 6a, q = 2a-b. Then r = p-q = 4a+b and s = 2q = 4a-2b.

Case IX: r = q, s = p-q.
- Then r+s = p and r-s = 2q-p, so B = pq(p-q)(2q-p).
- A/B = (p+q)/(2q-p) = a/b, so bp + bq = 2aq - ap and p/q = (2a-b)/(a+b).
- Take p = 2a-b, q = a+b. Then r = a+b and s = p-q = a-2b.

Case X: r = 2q, s = p-q.
- Then r+s = p+q and r-s = 3q-p, so B = 2q(p-q)(p+q)(3q-p).
- A/B = p/(6q-2p) = a/b, so bp = 6aq - 2ap and p/q = 6a/(b+2a).
- Take p = 6a, q = b+2a. Then r = 2b+4a and s = 4a-b.

Table of all ten (p,q,r,s):
- I: (a+b, 2a-b, a+b, 2b-a)
- II: (b-2a, 6a, 2b-4a, b+4a)
- III: (b+2a, 6a, 2b+4a, b-4a)
- IV: (a+b, b-2a, 2b-a, a+b)
- V: (2a+b, b-a, a+2b, b-a)
- VI: (6a, b-2a, 4a+b, 2b-4a)
- VII: (b+2a, a-b, 2b+a, a-b)
- VIII: (6a, 2a-b, b+4a, 4a-2b)
- IX: (2a-b, a+b, a+b, a-2b)
- X: (6a, b+2a, 2b+4a, 4a-b)

Rule for negative entries: if a generator comes out negative, replace it by its absolute value and give the larger number of each pair to p (resp. r). Justification (mine): A(p,q) changes only by sign under q -> -q or under p <-> q, so the ratio |A|:|B| is preserved.

Example 1 (a = b = 1).
- Cases I, III, IV, IX and X give identical or similar triangles; V and VII give q = 0 (degenerate).
- II, VI and VIII all reduce to p=6, q=1, r=5, s=2.
- These are the triangles 12-35-37 and 20-21-29, both of area 210.

Example 2 (a = 2, b = 1).
- Cases I, IV and IX are degenerate.
- II, VI and VIII give (12,3,9,6), with areas 4860 and 2430.
- III and X give (12,5,10,7), with areas 7140 and 3570.
- V and VII give (5,1,4,1), with areas 120 and 60.
- Euler then announces a reduced table of distinct solutions (continued on p.226).

My observation, consistent with the next page's reduction to I, V, II, III: up to sign changes and swapping p<->q and r<->s,
- IV and IX duplicate I,
- VII duplicates V,
- VI and VIII duplicate II,
- X duplicates III.
errors: No algebraic errors found: each of VIII, IX, X and all ten table rows satisfy b*A = a*B identically.

Example 2, solution (12,3,9,6): the pair (r,s) = (9,6) is not coprime, so the second triangle is a scaled copy (by 9) of the one from (3,2). This is harmless for a rational-triangle problem but not primitive.
The sign-conversion rule is stated without justification. It is valid because A(p,q) = -A(q,p) = -A(p,-q), so only signs of areas change; the ratio holds in absolute value.

results.what: Ten linear-substitution parametric families (p,q,r,s) in terms of a,b giving two Pythagorean triangles whose areas are in the ratio a:b
results.modern_name: Parametric solutions of the Diophantine equation b*pq(p^2-q^2) = a*rs(r^2-s^2), i.e. rational points on the corresponding quartic surface via linear substitutions
results.usually_credited_to: The problem class goes back to Diophantus, Fermat and Frenicle (17th c.); Euler treated equal-area and proportional-area triangles in several papers

results.what: Equal-area pair from a=b=1: generators (6,1) and (5,2), i.e. triangles 12-35-37 and 20-21-29, both of area 210

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine ad hoc linear substitutions for a classical Diophantine problem, published in Euler's Opera Postuma (1862). The method and examples are standard 18th-century fare and already attributed to him.

checkable.sympy: a,b=symbols('a b'); A=lambda p,q:p*q*(p**2-q**2); p,q,r,s=6*a,2*a-b,b+4*a,4*a-2*b; expand(b*A(p,q)-a*A(r,s))==0

checkable.asserts: All remaining table rows I-VII are correct
Example 2: area ratio 2 in each listed solution
